q-0017.answer: Muslims believe Allah revealed the Torah (Tawrat) to Moses, the Gospel (Injil) to Jesus, and the Quran to Muhammad ﷺ as the final preserved revelation (3:3, 5:46, 5:68). Earlier scriptures were sent for guidance though Muslims hold the Quran as the authoritative text today.

q-0633.answer:
Surah Al-Inshiqaaq (84) — The Splitting Open · 25 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• Splitting the Heavens asunder and stretching the Earth forth on the Day of Resurrection
• Inform them, O Muhammad, that Allah has prepared for them a painful torment.
• The Recompense for Deeds is True
• From their mannerism is rejection, obstinacy, and opposition to the truth.
• Certainly Allah will repeat his creation just as he began his creation, and He will reward him based upon his deeds, whether they were good or bad.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

q-0718.answer: Scholars classify the 114 surahs by where they were first revealed: approximately **86 surahs are Meccan** (revealed before Hijrah in Makkah) and **28 are Medinan** (revealed after Hijrah in Madinah). Meccan surahs often focus on faith, tawhid, and the Hereafter; Medinan surahs often address law, community, and governance. Individual surah pages show each surah's revelation type.
